title: Archived UC span links must be normalized against the preserved request ID
answers: After restoring an archived Unity Catalog trace, span links lose the catalog and schema
Why do links on a round-tripped UC trace no longer point to the right location?
Why does preserve_request_id strip the UC location from span links?
body:
Symptom: after a Unity Catalog trace is archived and read back with its request ID preserved, its span links no longer carry the `trace:/catalog.schema/` location.
Root cause: mlflow/entities/span.py:Span.from_otel_proto with preserve_request_id=True. Without a location_id the generated `tr-...` ID is used as mlflow_trace_id, and links were normalized against that, so the UC location was stripped.
Fix pattern: resolve the effective request ID first (the serialized REQUEST_ID attribute when preserve_request_id is set, otherwise the generated ID), normalize links against that value, and reuse the same value for the span's REQUEST_ID attribute.
Constraints: applies only on the preserve_request_id path; without it the location comes from location_id. Regression coverage is tests/entities/test_span.py:test_span_from_otel_proto_can_preserve_request_id_for_round_trip, which checks the OTLP bytes of the linked trace.
applies: Changes to Span.from_otel_proto or any code that rebuilds spans from OTLP with a preserved request ID; not for fresh span creation from live OTel spans.
says: Restoring an archived Unity Catalog trace strips the catalog and schema from span links
Span links on archived traces lose their destination path after being loaded back
Preserve the full catalog and schema location for links when round-tripping archived traces
Why do links between spans no longer navigate to the right catalog in saved traces
search: Archived Unity Catalog span links in mlflow/entities/span.py:Span.from_otel_proto must be normalized against the effective preserved request ID rather than a generated trace ID. When preserve_request_id is true, resolve the serialized REQUEST_ID attribute first, normalize links against it to retain the trace:/catalog.schema/ location, and assign it to the span REQUEST_ID. Applies to code rebuilding spans from OTLP with preserve_request_id=True, but not to fresh span creation from live OpenTelemetry spans where locations derive from location_id. Verified by tests/entities/test_span.py:test_span_from_otel_proto_can_preserve_request_id_for_round_trip on linked trace OTLP bytes.
